name: Referral ask
description: Asks someone to point you at the right person. Makes the ask small and specific — a name, not an introduction — because a name costs ten seconds and an introduction costs social capital.
audience: People adjacent to your buyer: former colleagues of theirs, advisors, or anyone who plainly knows the person you actually need.

variants: {{firstName|Hi}} — you sit right in the middle of a network I'm trying to understand. Connecting; I'd value your read on something small.
Hi {{firstName|there}} — you know the people I'm trying to reach far better than I do. Happy to connect and ask one short question.
Thanks {{firstName|there}}. One question, ten seconds: who at {{company|a company like yours}} actually owns this decision? A name is plenty — I'll do the rest myself.
Small ask, {{firstName|there}}: who would you go to about this if you were me? Just a name, no introduction needed.
{{firstName|Hi}} — no obligation at all. If it's easier to say "not my area", that's a genuinely useful answer too.
Happy to hear "I don't know", {{firstName|there}} — it saves me guessing. And if there's anything I can point you at in return, say so.
Leaving it there, {{firstName|there}} — thanks for connecting regardless. Happy to return the favour any time.
I'll stop asking, {{firstName|there}}. If I can ever be useful in the other direction, just ask.
